name: Uttar Pradesh
summary_text: Uttar Pradesh hosts the most trans-visible public space in India: the Kinnar Akhara (trans/hijra monastic order) fielded a Mahamandaleshwar — one of its highest-ranking monks — at the head of 15 trans spiritual leaders in ceremonial bathing at the Maha Kumbh in Prayagraj (Jan-Feb 2025), the world's largest religious gathering, in a collaboration with the Naga Sadhus/Aghori grouping in the making since 2015. A trans visitor at the Kumbh is inside an institutionally recognised religious hierarchy, not a marginalised underground. The inclusion is contested, however: a rival leadership instalment drew protests from within the community and other sects, gurus threatened to boycott the 2037 Kumbh, and a top-ranking trans monk who objected was physically attacked on 12 February 2025. UP also has a constituted welfare board. Against the national 0.43, UP sits +0.03. The Kinnar Akhara inclusion is visitor-facing, seasonal, and institutionally validated by the broader Akharas' governance structures, but the festival-week attack and boycott threats show the recognition is contested rather than settled. A further counterweight exists — a single transgender woman, Kajal, was strangled in Kanpur (Aug 2025) during a robbery — but this is a lone incident with no patterned state-actor response and does not constitute a regional finding under the single-incident rule. Compared to Tamil Nadu (0.53), UP lacks a comprehensive policy framework or judicial endorsement; compared to Maharashtra (0.38), UP does not show the festival-entry religion-screening that creates outing mechanisms at public gatherings. The net positive is narrow and temporally concentrated.

sources.title: World’s Largest Religious Gathering Becomes Trans-Inclusive | Inter Press Service
sources.claim_summary: IPS report (18 Feb 2025): at the Maha Kumbh in Prayagraj, Pavitra Nandagiri, a Mahamandaleshwar of the Kinnar Akhara (transgender monastic order), joined 15 trans spiritual leaders in the 12 February 2025 ceremonial bathing alongside Naga Sadhus and Aghoris; the arrangement, in the making since 2015, is disputed — a leadership appointment triggered protests, some gurus threatened to boycott the 2037 Kumbh, and senior trans monk Kalyani Nandagiri was attacked on 12 February 2025.

sources.title: Remembering Our Dead - Kajal (10 Aug 2025)
sources.claim_summary: NOTE: page not retrievable at fetch time (never cached); the underlying Transrespect-versus-Transphobia case report (10 Aug 2025) documents Kajal, a 25-year-old trans woman, and her 12-year-old adopted brother strangled by intruders at their home in Yogendra Vihar, Kanpur, during a robbery; the suspect died by suicide.

sources.title: Constitution of Transgender Welfare Boards/Commissions
sources.claim_summary: Press Information Bureau reply in the Rajya Sabha (8 Dec 2021, Minister Dr. Virendra Kumar): 12 states/UTs have constituted Transgender Welfare Boards under section 10(1) of the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Rules, 2020 - Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Gujarat, Rajasthan, Chandigarh, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, West Bengal, Tripura and Mizoram.
